sources.citation: Conrad, Robert J. & T. Wayne Dye. 1975. Some language relationships in the Upper Sepik region of Papua New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 18 (Pacific Linguistics A-40), 1-35. Canberra: ANU. hdl 1885/254341.
sources.note: p.9: Nakwi treated as a dialect of Nimo ('The Nakwi dialect contains 71% probable cognates with Nimo. Villages identified with this dialect are Nakwi-Amasu and Augot (Mumupra, Sari).'). p.10 Figure C 'Summary of Arai Phonology' (family-level, verified on page image): 'Contrastive word stress was noted in Ama, and possibly in Rocky Peak, Bo, and Owiniga.' Nimo/Nakwi not named; nothing on stress placement in Nimo or Nakwi. Table 2 wordlists have a Nimo column only (no Nakwi column) and carry no stress marks.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1975. Sko, Kwomtari, and Left May (Arai) phyla. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1 (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 849-858. hdl 1885/252979.
sources.note: p.855 lists 'Nimo (Nimo-Wasuai, Nakwi) 413' and says 'Insufficient data is available on the typological features of the group, although Conrad and Dye give an outline of phonological features'. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1973. Sepik languages: checklist and preliminary classification. Pacific Linguistics B-25. Canberra: ANU. hdl 1885/146478.
sources.note: p.45 entry 167 NAKWI (verified on page image): 'SIL lists from Nakwi (=Naukwi-Amasu), Mumupra and Aukot (=Augot) identify this language as part of the Left May group, but little more is known.' Nothing on phonology or stress.
